profile.headline: React Dev, Team Lead and Accessibility Expert
profile.summary:
An experienced software engineer with over 30 years (yikes!!!) of experience, working in Ireland, Spain, Canada, and the USA, for everything from small startups to multinationals like Microsoft, Cisco, and Symantec. 

An entrepreneur who developed and eventually sold a small tech company called ToolProof in 2000.

I’ve always had a passion for software done right. I love solving problems, big or small. I love being part of the process of rearing software – from MVP to making it gradually better and better, micro-architecting as you go, maintaining quality while meeting timelines, and helping your baby grow and prosper. 

I’ve worked on server and client, desktop and web. My passions come out a lot more in front-end development. I love to see the fruits of my labor and see other people use my creations. I started my career in Symantec as a Localization Tools Developer, where my co-workers in the localization department used my tools to do their jobs every day, and that direct connection with my users helped me develop into an engineer with a passion for good UI and good UX. 

In the last decade, I migrated to web development. And, in the last several years, I have become an expert in Digital Accessibility. 90% of the web fails WCAG compliance – part of that 90% was developed by me. But now I know a lot better, and making accessible UI is a foundational requirement for everything I create. 

All accessibility experts know that part of the job is looking after yourself, and part is making sure everyone else joins in. UX, dev, QA, product, marketing… hardware and software. I have morphed from a software engineer to a company leader, looking after all aspects of accessibility. I've helped close sales that depended on A11Y compliance, and guide architects and engineers on site design for EV charging installations. I've worked on VPAT audits, assisted the policy team with Access Board requirements. I've hosted workshops and training sessions, and even presented at the company all-hands and other company-wide events.

I love it – I love the influence I now have at the corporate level. But, I’m still a software engineer at heart.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.locationName: Santa Clara, California, United States · On-site
positions.description: React web development for OSMO platform in NVIDIA Robotics team.

positions.title: Senior Staff Engineer Frontend (React) & Accessibility Architect
positions.description:
I look after everything Accessibility related in ChargePoint. 

From working with the policy team on #EVSE accessibility requirements to helping out on RFPs and sales inquiries that relate to either station or software accessibility compliance. 

I am a developer at heart, so everything I do (I lead the dev team for ChargePoint's driver website) has to be accessible. And, as ChargePoint's digital accessibility expert, I also help ensure that everyone else follows suit. 

From training, best practices, and organizing workshops, to badgering and reminding everyone of our commitment to #a11y, I find that I have my hands in many different aspects of ChargePoint's current business and future plans. 

90% of the web is inaccessible. We need to change that, and changing that requires changing how we develop software. That's my job!!!

positions.title: Senior Staff Software Engineer (React)
positions.description:
ChargePoint driver portal and admin portal provide industry-leading capabilities to its millions of users. 

I look after ChargePoint's driver website. The current incarnation was released in Jan 2023 and was ChargePoint's first #WCAG compliant product. 

I was lead developer for that multi-year rewrite of the old PHP portal (yuck!!) and am very proud of what we achieved. We have over 1 million drivers in the ChargePoint eco system. 

I personally solved a lot of the accessibility problems and developed an accessible component's library called cp-toolkit along the way. There's a lot happening, in the map page in particular. Some of the things I'm most proud of are our screen reader experience, the fact that 100% of functionality can be achieved without the use of a mouse, and, most of all... everything is usable (and pretty decent) at 400% zoom - that's a full map and list of stations in the top 1/3 of your mobile screen!
I lead the UI team responsible for redesigning the portals to support accessibility, ease of localization, international expansion including RTL languages and a more modern look and feel. The current code-base is a combination of PHP, Angular and JS. New portal code is written in React. We have to be familiar with all and comfortable merging these two worlds together as we continue to support the old code-base while rewriting it into something that ChargePoint can use for the decade to come.

After what we learned in the development of the driver portal, I extended my role to help the rest of ChargePoint follow suit - a position which I continue to own today.

positions.title: App developer - Xbox 360, XBOX One, SamsungTV, Web
positions.description:
Cisco acquired 1Mainstream in 2015. I continued as lead for the devices team, with my concentration now on HTML Streaming Devices. 

I designed the architecture for a complete re-write, creating a single code-base, written in JavaScript, jQuery and HTML that runs across a range of devices including SamsungTV, Playstation, XBOX One, Windows10, OperaTV, LGTV and PanasonicTV. Our custom-built MVC framework includes componentization of device specific functionality, a navigation framework that supports the various input modalities of the different devices and a model that works with multiple 'channels' and is used by YES StingTV (Israel), NFL Sunday Ticket and more.
positions.insights: Skills: Software Development · JavaScript · Software Engineering · C# · Xbox 360

positions.title: UI Technical Team Lead, NOOK for Windows 8. C#/XAML Developer
positions.description:
Technical lead for the Windows 8 NOOK e-reader application. I have lead the team through 5 product releases which have seen us move from a 2.5* rated app to our current 4.2* rating. NOOK is the highest rated reading app for Windows 8, ahead of Kindle, Zinio, Kobo, etc. 

Coding is in C# and XAML. Development process is Agile. I split my time about 50-50 between team lead tasks and actual development work. I am heavily involved with product planning, costing and scheduling, as well as getting the most out of my team.
positions.insights: Skills: Software Development · C# · Organizational Leadership · Windows 8 · App Development

positions.title: UI Software Development Lead. C++ Windows Developer
positions.description:
Sococo is a virtual office environment which provides people with their own office and a communications back-end that allows them to interact with their virtual colleagues with IM, voice, video and app-sharing. 

I lead a distributed team of Mac and Windows developers. We used an Agile development process focused on small incremental releases on all platforms. I was responsible for the prioritization of new features and bug fixes as well as cross-team collaboration with the server and platform teams. Coding is in C++. I split my time about 70-30 between coding and team lead activities.
positions.insights: Skills: C# · Software Engineering · Startups · C++

positions.title: Senior Development Engineer – C#, WPF,C++, AD, WMI, POWERSHELL
positions.description:
Involvement in the full SDLC of 4 releases of Microsoft Lync Server, working mainly in the area of manageability and software deployment. I was one of the key players in the multi-year, multi-release redesign of Lync Server to work in a hosted environment in Microsoft's data centers. I also owned the deployment UI (C#/WPF) and lead the manageability team’s efforts to auto-deploy and manage Lync Server to thousands of servers in the data center. 

Key skills:
•	Developing Powershell cmdlets
•	Expert C# and OO design skills
•	WDS and POWERSHELL
•	Active Directory development and debugging
•	Server programming concepts such as WMI, User Rights Management and Active Directory
positions.insights: Skills: Software Development · C# · Software Engineering

positions.title: Software Consultant – C#, ASPX.NET, HTML, SQL
positions.description:
• Primarily Visual C# .NET Web development of dynamic, database driven websites using SQL Server in the back-end to produce various projects, mainly for the Ontario Ministry of Health 
  o Portal site for Long-Term-Care Homes
  o Long-Term-Care Homes Exceptional Circumstances
  o Long-Term-Care Homes Staff Survey
  o Social Housing Services Corporation Portal Site
  o Social Housing Services Corporation Best Practices Application
  o MOHCIB Publication System

• Involved in all stages of the SDLC, from gathering client requirements through to user and technical specifications, time estimations, database design, software development, QA, client training, documentation and support. Specifications were done using Visio flow-charts. 

Skills:
• Expert in C# ASPX.NET development – 3 ½ years experience
• Intermediate experience of SQL
positions.insights: Skills: Software Development · C# · Software Engineering

positions.title: Founder and C++ developer; localization expert
positions.description:
I developed and successfully sold a QA automation tool called ToolProof which tested the UI of running applications and was a huge hit in the localization arena. Customers included Novell, Corel, Symantec, Visio, FileNET and Canon (C++, MFC). Developing and marketing my own product helped me to grow both professionally and personally and I learned a lot about dealing with people and about business in general, from forecasting and creating business plans to partnership agreements and dealing with accountants and solicitors. 

I also worked as a consultant for various companies in Dublin:

• QA Partners - Implemented automated UI testing algorithms in Segue Silk

• Corel - Integrated ToolProof into a QA automated environment via Visual Test

• Localization Resource Center - Analysis, design and development of an EC funded project called TransRouter (Visual C++/Access)

• Trados– QA Lead for Trados Translation Memory

• FIT College – Development of the curriculum for the new localization engineering course that the college was starting and training of the teachers who were to give the course 

• Ericsson LMI– Developed a small database add-on to Ericsson’s FraudOffice system

• Post Consult International – Lead developer on various encryption based projects
  o Facilitated the use of AIB (Ireland’s largest Bank) bank cards through Post Office terminals, using a HSM for encryption, digital signing and secure data transfer in a large, multi-tier application
  o Developed the system to come up with the winning numbers for the Prize Bonds (Irish lottery) – random number generation, secure ftp, encryption and digital signing (Baltimore Technologies)
  o Highly secure environment with strict code reviews, and all code had to be verified and digitally signed before sign-off

• Vistatec – various projects for the localization tools department of Vistatec, all written in C#
positions.insights: Skills: Software Development · Organizational Leadership · Software Engineering · C++

positions.title: Software Developer / Localization Tools Expert (Visual C++)
positions.description:
• Principal developer of Symantec's in-house, industry leading localization tools (resource editor, resource comparison tool and resource update tools). 

• Contributed greatly to the localization process both in Symantec and in the industry in general. I grew to become one of the top localization experts in Ireland while at the same time gaining fluency in MFC and technical expertise in Windows messaging and under-the-cover Windows features such as the binary format of EXEs and DLLs. 

• Lead of a small team of three developers

• Process analysis of Symantec’s development practices from a localization perspective

• Training users worldwide, including several trips to the U.S. to educate developers and QA on localization best practices

• Localization analysis of any new acquisitions Symantec was making or considering making (e.g. Norton Ghost)

• DBCS enabling of Norton Administrator for Networks and Norton Anti-Virus for the Japanese market
positions.insights: Skills: Software Development · Organizational Leadership · Software Engineering · C++
